html:
The Kingdom of Sind was the realm of the lower Indus ruled from Aror by the Brahman dynasty, from about 632 until the Arab conquest of 712.

The dynasty began when Chach, a Brahmin minister of the last Rai king, took the throne. His kingdom stretched from the coast to the borders of Kashmir and toward Makran in the west. Its people were Buddhist and Hindu, and the Indus was busy with river and sea trade.

In 711 and 712, the Umayyad general Muhammad bin Qasim invaded on behalf of the Umayyad Caliphate. Chach's son, Raja Dahir, was killed in battle, and Sind became a province of the caliphate; see the Arab conquest of Sindh. Much of the story comes from the Chach Nama, a Persian history written in the 13th century. For the region later, see Sindh.
sum: The Kingdom of Sind was the realm of the lower Indus ruled from Aror by the Brahman dynasty, from about 632 until the Arab conquest of 712.
